result:
`./compile.sh` reports success. I wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFormatAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering:

- All 12 predefined format constants (`DEFAULT`, `EXCEL`, `RFC4180`, `MYSQL`, `ORACLE`, `POSTGRESQL_CSV/TEXT`, `MONGODB_CSV/TSV`, `INFORMIX_UNLOAD(_CSV)`, `TDF`) against their documented settings
- `newFormat(char)` initial state and its line-break rejection
- `valueOf(String)` happy path, unknown-name, and null-arg cases
- `CSVFormat.Predefined` (`values()`, `valueOf()`, `getFormat()` linkage)
- `Builder`: fluent chaining, `create()`/`create(format)`, `get()`/`build()`, `Supplier` interface, every setter/getter round trip, defensive array copying for header/header comments, and documented `IllegalArgumentException` cases (comment marker/escape line breaks)
- `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString` contract basics, immutability of static constants
- Package-private helpers (`copy()`, `copy(CSVFormat)`, `clone(T...)`, `getDelimiterCharArray()`, `getEscapeChar()`)
- Deprecated `withX` methods and their documented exceptions
- `format`, `println`, `printRecord`, `print(Object, Appendable, boolean)`, `print`/`printer`/`parse` return-value checks
